title: Length Using Non-Standard Units
introduction: Explore length using non-standard units using everyday examples.
definition: Measure length by placing equal-sized objects end to end without gaps or overlaps. Use the same unit when comparing lengths.

visuals.label: Six equal blocks
visuals.alt: Six equal blocks — Measure without gaps.

examples.question: A pencil covers six equal blocks.

exercises.question: A ribbon covers 8 blocks and another covers 5. Which is longer? Enter block count.
exercises.solution: 8 > 5, so the ribbon covering 8 blocks is longer when the blocks are equal.

exercises.question: A line covers 7 equal clips. Length in clips?
exercises.solution: Count the seven equal clips placed end to end: 7 clips.

exercises.question: Two lines cover 6 and 4 blocks. Difference?
Should units have equal length? yes/no
exercises.solution: Equal-length units make the measurements consistent and comparable.

exercises.question: Should there be gaps between units? yes/no
exercises.solution: Gaps leave part of the length unmeasured, so place units end to end.

exercises.question: A book is 3 hand spans long. Another is 2 hand spans using the same hand. Total spans?

summary: Measure length by placing equal-sized objects end to end without gaps or overlaps. Use the same unit when comparing lengths.
